description: Re-run of the 6 worst-performing filings from the original 16-filing batch (manifest.json), using a revised prompt (extraction_prompt_v2.txt) that explicitly warns against amount-bracket legends, forbids inventing illegible names, and forbids installing other tools. Run 2026-09-24, same session as the original batch's follow-up work. Every `v2_verify_extraction_result` below is the real, literal output of calling `scan_verification.verify_extraction()` against the parsed extraction (not a hand-reasoned guess) -- confirmed by actually running it against these six files.
conclusion: Modest, uneven improvement -- not a fix. One clear win (the McCaul legend-confusion case), one new regression (a previously-honest empty result became a confidently wrong non-empty one), and one important non-content finding (a multi-page PDF that the headless Read tool may only be seeing page 1 of). scan_verification.verify_extraction()'s blank-description check is doing real work here: it independently catches 2 of the 6 filings below (9107579, 9111845) that would otherwise have written bad data.

filings.v1_verdict: BAD (fabricated company names: 'Malt Cocktail Wines Inc.', 'Tar Brands Inc.')
filings.v2_verify_extraction_result: ok=False, needs_review=False -- rejected: 2 of 6 rows have a blank asset_description_raw
filings.notes: No fabricated names this time -- real companies (Analog Devices, Emerson Electric, General Electric, Parker Hannifin). But coverage dropped (10 -> 6) and 2 rows now have a null description instead of a plausible-but-wrong one. Net effect: less confidently wrong, but still incomplete, and still correctly rejected by verify_extraction rather than silently written.

filings.v1_verdict: BAD (missed all of page 1, amounts off by multiple brackets)
filings.notes: Different 4 rows than v1 (now includes Procter & Gamble), ground truth is 6-8 -- still an undercount, still page-1 content apparently missing. owner is null on every row. Prompt v2 did not fix the multi-page coverage gap.

filings.v1_verdict: FAILED (honest empty result, model said scan quality too poor)
filings.v2_verify_extraction_result: ok=False, needs_review=True -- rejected: 7 of 7 rows blank, PLUS flagged: a single (owner, description, type, date, amount) combination repeats 4 times
filings.notes: REGRESSION in behavior, not caught by the ground truth count alone: v1's honest 'I can't read this' became v2's confident 7-row array with every description blank -- the exact legend-confusion shape the v2 prompt was written to prevent, on a *different* filing than the one it was written for. verify_extraction() catches this outright, which is the whole point of having it as an independent gate rather than trusting prompt engineering alone.

filings.v1_verdict: FAILED (tried to run apt-get install poppler-utils, refused, gave up)
filings.v2_verify_extraction_result: ok=True, needs_review=True -- flagged: zero transactions extracted
filings.notes: No longer tries to install a forbidden tool (the explicit instruction worked), but reveals a more fundamental issue instead: the model's own explanation says the headless Read tool only surfaced page 1 of this multi-page PDF, and it had no way to reach later pages under the allowed tool set. Worth investigating directly (e.g. whether Read needs an explicit page-range hint in headless mode) before assuming a prompt fix alone can solve this filing.

filings.v1_verdict: BAD (silent data corruption -- the amount-bracket legend (columns A-K) extracted as 14 transactions, every description null)
filings.v2_verify_extraction_result: ok=True, needs_review=False (n=20 is exactly at, not over, the >20 review threshold)
filings.notes: Clear win: real company names (ABBVIE INC/ABBV, ACCENTURE PLC/ACN, ADOBE INC, ...), no blank descriptions, no legend confusion. The explicit 'a legend is not a transaction table' instruction appears to have worked for the exact failure mode it targeted. Still very likely an undercount against the ~100+ ground truth (this filing has 6 dense pages) -- the mechanical checks here can't catch under-extraction, only garbage rows, so this filing still needs a human page-count sanity check before being trusted.

filings.v1_verdict: FAILED (empty, handwritten filing, gave up even with a longer timeout)
filings.v2_verify_extraction_result: ok=True, needs_review=False -- passes today, but tx_type/tx_date/amount_min/amount_max are all null, which no current check flags; worth a future check for 'too many null fields on a non-empty row'
filings.notes: Partial win: extracted one transaction ('T-BILL') matching the ground truth count of 1, where v1 gave up entirely. Most other fields are still null. The 'attempt a careful reading rather than giving up' instruction seems to have helped the model try, even if the result is incomplete.

recommendations: Keep verify_extraction()'s blank-description check as a hard gate -- it independently caught real problems in 2 of these 6 filings under the *improved* prompt, including a new failure shape the prompt change itself introduced on a different filing.

Investigate the apparent multi-page Read-tool limitation (house:9114491) directly before assuming further prompt tuning will fix RISKY-tier multi-page filings -- this may be a tooling/invocation issue, not a content-understanding one.

Add an under-extraction signal for large filings: none of the mechanical checks in verify_extraction() catch a plausible-looking but incomplete result (house:8218645's 20-of-100+ and house:9107699's 4-of-6-8). A rough page-count-to-transaction-count ratio, or a required model self-report of 'total rows visible', would help.

Do not treat this prompt revision as validated -- one more filing (9111845) got mechanically worse under it. This needs a larger sample before being adopted as the production prompt, not a 6-filing spot check.
